headline: Reference-free DockQ-style scoring compares protein interfaces across MD frames
label: Protein Interface Quality Assessment
summary: Reference-free interface scoring for MD frames arrives alongside new tools for binding free energy and covalent ligand interactions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative assessment of protein-protein interface geometry. MDQ adapts DockQ-style logic into a symmetric, reference-free score that compares interfaces across molecular dynamics frames and yields a distance metric for clustering conformations. Its novelty is that interface similarity is computed without a reference structure, so conformations can be compared directly from simulation output. The remaining items are heterogeneous and only loosely related to this thread: BFEE3 provides absolute binding free energy calculations with an AI assistant and new DDM protocols, CovPDB 2.0 expands a covalent protein-ligand database to about 6200 complexes, CNR computes contact-network responsiveness descriptors for 22,167 human proteins, and a preprint pipeline combines transcriptomics and docking to identify human targets of plastic-derived chemicals. Their outputs and data types differ from MDQ, so their results are not directly comparable to its interface metric.
